subsystems.name: Seed payload
subsystems.role: the compact starter kit that lands first and contains everything needed to begin building.

subsystems.name: Regolith handling
subsystems.role: digs up, sorts and feeds local soil so no material has to be launched.

subsystems.name: Swarm robots
subsystems.role: many small machines that cooperate instead of one large builder.

subsystems.name: Structural shell
subsystems.role: the load-bearing and shielding envelope, made from sintered or cemented soil.
parts: printed or sintered dome or vault

subsystems.name: Pressure envelope
subsystems.role: the sealed part that actually holds breathable air; the soil shell itself does not.

subsystems.name: Power and control
subsystems.role: keeps the build running through the two-week lunar night.
parts: solar array plus batteries or a small fission reactor

buildSteps.title: Characterise the site
buildSteps.detail: Orbital and rover data establish soil grain size, chemistry, slope and whether ice is present, since those dictate which binding method will work.

buildSteps.title: Land the seed payload
buildSteps.detail: A lander sets down a printer head, several small robots, a power supply and a control computer in one compact package.

buildSteps.title: Clear and gather soil
buildSteps.detail: Robots level a pad and excavate regolith, screening out coarse rock and feeding a hopper.

buildSteps.title: Build the shell
buildSteps.detail: The printer lays down soil mixed with a binder, or sinters it directly with microwaves, layer by layer into a dome or vault, typically over an inflated former.

buildSteps.title: Place the pressure liner
buildSteps.detail: An inflatable bladder or welded liner goes inside the shell and is sealed to the airlock; the liner holds the air, the soil holds the structure and blocks radiation.

buildSteps.title: Cover for shielding
buildSteps.detail: Further layers of loose or sintered regolith are piled over the shell to cut radiation and micrometeorite risk.

buildSteps.title: Fit services
buildSteps.detail: Power cables, life support, thermal control and the airlock are connected and tested.

buildSteps.title: Pressurise and commission
buildSteps.detail: The habitat is leak-tested, filled with air and handed over; the robots then start a second module, growing the base incrementally.

prerequisites.why: oxygen has been extracted from simulated regolith in labs, but turning soil into reliable structural material at scale is unproven.
microwave sintering and binder jetting of simulants have been demonstrated on Earth; nobody has printed a structure in lunar vacuum.
swarms work in labs and warehouses, but unsupervised construction on an airless surface is a different problem.
landing tonnes rather than kilograms of printer and robot hardware is still rare.
a self-building habitat is pointless if it still needs constant resupply of air, water and food.

pathway.milestone: Earth-based printing of habitat shells from simulants and volcanic rock, plus robot construction trials
pathway.unlocks: proof that soil-based printing can be structurally sound.

pathway.milestone: a small sintering or printing experiment on the lunar surface
pathway.unlocks: real data on how soil behaves in vacuum, low gravity and wide temperature swings.

pathway.milestone: an uncrewed printed shelter that survives a lunar night
pathway.unlocks: confidence that robots can build something bigger than a test coupon.

pathway.milestone: a crew-rated printed habitat, then repeatable modular expansion
pathway.unlocks: bases that grow without shipping every wall from Earth.

pathway.milestone: the same approach adapted to Martian soil
pathway.unlocks: habitats for long-duration surface missions and eventual settlements.
